memory_candidates: Lean 4 Relation.ReflTransGen gotcha: `induction`/`cases` on a `Relation.ReflTransGen r a b` hypothesis auto-generalizes any locally-bound `b` it depends on, renaming it to a fresh inaccessible variable per case (the pre-existing local `b` becomes an unrelated leftover). Use `rename_i` immediately after entering a case and verify via `lean_goal` which fresh name plays which role before writing the rest of the branch -- do not assume the original variable name is still live.

Lean 4 rfl-substitution direction gotcha (generalizes an earlier-recorded lesson): `rcases h with rfl | ...` on an equation between two PRE-EXISTING local variables (not a freshly-`intro`'d one) can substitute in either direction and is not predictable from binder order alone -- observed eliminating the OLDER variable in favor of the newer one. Use a named `heq` and explicit `rw [heq]` instead of `rfl` whenever both sides of the equation are pre-existing variables referenced elsewhere in context.

Lean 4 well-founded recursion pattern: for a 'raise a node + its finite forward-reachable closure through a Finset of children' style recursion (tree-cascade lifting lemmas), `Set.ncard {q ∈ X | ht q ≥ ht p}` (using an existing graded-rank function) is a clean, easy-to-work-with strictly-decreasing measure for the recursive call on each child -- avoids constructing a bespoke BFS-distance function. Disjointness of different children's downward closures follows from a single `huniq`-style unique-parent application at the LAST edge of whichever path would witness an overlap -- no general cycle-freeness/BFS-uniqueness lemma is needed.
